draft.title: The Michelson-Morley experiment
card: Before 1900, many physicists thought light was a wave that travelled through a medium called the aether. They thought the aether filled all of space and sat at rest.
If the aether existed, Earth would move through it. Light travelling along Earth's motion would then have a different measured speed from light travelling across it.

In 1887, Michelson and Morley split a light beam into two beams at right angles and compared them. They looked for a shift in the pattern made when the beams recombined. They found no shift that matched Earth's motion.
So the measured speed of light did not change with Earth's motion, and no aether was detected. This result fits special relativity, which says light has the same speed for all observers.
draft.remember: No change in the speed of light was found, so no aether was detected.

a.q: What did Michelson and Morley's experiment find?
opts: The speed of light did not depend on Earth's motion
The speed of light was greater along Earth's motion
The speed of light was less along Earth's motion
The speed of light changed with the time of year
a.why: They looked for a difference in light's speed in different directions relative to Earth's motion and found none. The tempting option about a greater speed along the motion is what the aether idea predicted, but it was not seen.
a.clue: Think about what the aether idea predicted, then what was actually seen.

b.q: A student says the experiment supports special relativity. Which reason is correct?
opts: The result fits light having the same speed for all observers
The result shows light needs a medium to travel through
The result shows Earth is at rest in the aether
The result shows light speeds up in a moving frame
b.why: Finding no change in light's speed with Earth's motion fits the idea that light has the same speed for all observers. The option about Earth at rest in the aether is tempting, but the experiment detected no aether at all.
b.clue: Which option matches a null result, with no aether found?
